context: Two mechanical cleanups, one PR. For (2), keep the adapter-side function (platforms/motherduck.py) as the canonical one and import it in the credentials module, or hoist to a small shared helper - avoid an import cycle (credentials/motherduck.py already imports the adapter lazily inside validate).
description: Found 2026-07-31 during the credential-egress review. (1) benchbox/utils/input_validation.py:585 sanitize_error_message has ZERO production call sites (only its own unit tests reference it) and despite its security-suggestive name it redacts table/column/database/schema identifiers, NOT credentials - it inflates any inventory of 'redaction implementations' and invites false confidence. Remove it and its tests (wiring it up is the wrong direction: real credential scrubbing lives in the anonymization/platform_options layer). (2) _redact_motherduck_token (benchbox/platforms/motherduck.py:53) and _redact_token (benchbox/platforms/credentials/motherduck.py:147) are copy-paste duplicates of the same regex+replace logic - the exact single-source-of-truth failure mode that let the secret-key lists diverge. Keep one implementation and import it from the other site.
